finding: Byte-integrity verification and semantic role binding existed as separate fail-closed verifiers, but no committed composition layer enforced their order or preserved stage-specific failure evidence.
design_implication: Promotion tooling should call one chain entry point that runs byte retention verification first, semantic binding second, rejects stage disagreement, and never represents semantic verification when byte verification failed.

verification.environment: isolated Node runtime reconstructed from committed dependency sources
cases: accept only when byte and semantic stages both pass
stop at byte failure without claiming semantic verification
preserve successful byte evidence when semantic binding fails
reject cross-commit semantic payload after valid byte binding

uncertainty: Not executed against an authenticated real repository evidence set.
Not integrated into the retained-evidence CLI or Vercel promotion path in this slice.
No deployment or workflow-completeness claim is made.
falsification_route: Run the chain against a real seven-role retained evidence set and demonstrate either a stage-order bypass, an accepted cross-commit payload, or a divergence between the chain result and its two constituent verifiers.
privacy: No credentials, private logs, personal data, or unpublished source material retained.
